subject: art-design
title: Critical Analysis Terms: Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch your vocabulary: iconography, formalism, context and beyond.
meta_desc: Stretch GCSE analysis: iconography, formalism, narrative, allegory, context.
final_note: These words turn description into informed criticism.

concepts.def: Identifying and interpreting symbols in art.
Analysis based on form, not subject or context.
A story implied or told by an artwork.
Whole work standing for a larger moral idea.
Category of subject e.g. portrait, still life.
Social, historical setting around the work.

walkthroughs.body_html: Iconography identifies symbols and decodes them. A lamb in Christian Renaissance art is rarely just a lamb — it stands for Christ. Iconography needs research into the time and place a work was made.

Formalism looks only at how the work is made — line, shape, colour — ignoring the artist's biography. Context insists the work cannot be understood without social and historical setting. Strong essays use both.

A narrative work tells a story — a moment frozen from a longer event. An allegory goes further: the whole work stands in for a moral or political idea. Delacroix's Liberty Leading the People (1830) is both.
